classification.difficultyReason: Introduce an unsuggested common ratio and discover both an ordinary sum and an x-, y-, z-weighted sum whose cyclic terms cancel, then connect zero logarithms to the two product identities.

content.prompt:
If $x$ and $y$ are distinct positive numbers, $a>0$, $a\ne1$ and
$$\frac{\log_a x}{y-z}=\frac{\log_a y}{z-x}=\frac{\log_a z}{x-y},$$
show that $xyz=1$ and $x^x y^y z^z=1$.

answer.short:
$xyz=1$ and $x^x y^y z^z=1$.

Set the common ratio equal to $k$. Add the three logarithmic equations, then add them after multiplying by $x$, $y$ and $z$, respectively.
answer.worked:
Let the common ratio be $k$. Then
$$\begin{align*}\log_a x&=k(y-z)\\\log_a y&=k(z-x)\\\log_a z&=k(x-y).\end{align*}$$
Adding and using the product law,
$$\begin{align*}\log_a(xyz)&=k(y-z+z-x+x-y)\\\log_a(xyz)&=0\\xyz&=a^0\\xyz&=1.\end{align*}$$
Using the power and product laws,
$$\begin{align*}\log_a(x^x y^y z^z)&=x\log_a x+y\log_a y+z\log_a z\\\log_a(x^x y^y z^z)&=k\bigl[x(y-z)+y(z-x)+z(x-y)\bigr]\\\log_a(x^x y^y z^z)&=k(xy-xz+yz-xy+xz-yz)\\\log_a(x^x y^y z^z)&=0\\x^x y^y z^z&=a^0\\x^x y^y z^z&=1.\end{align*}$$
